## The problem

AI coding agents can produce useful work, but a scientific software project also needs durable state, explicit permissions, reproducible tests, independent review and a clear boundary around human authority.

Dev Autopilot turns those requirements into a workflow instead of relying on one long prompt or one agent grading its own work.

## Authority is separated

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A[Project charter] --> B[Milestone]
    B --> C[Implementation]
    C --> D[Deterministic gates]
    D --> E[Adversarial audit]
    E --> F[Independent review]
    F --> G[Bounded correction]
    G --> D
    F --> H[Milestone acceptance]
    H --> B
    H --> I[Ready for human release]
```

Planning advice is not approval. The implementation agent cannot approve its own diff. Review agents cannot override mechanical gates. The system stops at `READY_FOR_HUMAN_RELEASE`, leaving commit, pull-request, tag and merge decisions to a person.

Review conclusions are bound to the exact repository diff they were written against. Any later change invalidates them, and unresolved or invalidated P0/P1 findings block milestone acceptance.

## Continuous project execution

A project starts from an immutable charter: mission, definition of done, non-goals, autonomy policy and a dependency-checked milestone DAG. `ask_questions: false` is enforced by the schema, so the workflow runs to completion on safe, reversible defaults rather than stopping to ask.

When it genuinely cannot proceed, it writes a machine-readable blocker with one required action and an explicit resume condition, instead of a conversational question nobody is there to answer.

## What persists

SQLite records:

- every legal state transition;
- append-only events and stop reasons;
- retry counts for each agent role;
- findings, reviews, assumptions and evidence;
- quota pauses and exact resume states;
- idempotency hashes and diff-keyed review caches;
- expiring exclusive run locks, leases, heartbeats and fencing tokens.

This allows a workflow to recover after process restarts without guessing where it left off.

## Safety design

Version 0.6.0 includes:

- validated YAML/JSON contracts with unknown fields rejected;
- scope, test, context-size and Git-metadata gates;
- bounded gate autocorrection instead of a terminal failure when an implementation can be repaired;
- fail-closed transitions and a fail-closed milestone acceptance decision;
- repository-bounded, read-only audit instructions with schema-constrained report output;
- deterministic jitter, short linear retry backoff and quota-reset support;
- bounded review and correction rounds;
- verified review bundles: JSON payloads, a human-readable HTML report and a folded digest;
- fake adapters for complete offline integration tests, including a simulated Drive API.

Real execution requires an explicit network opt-in. Shell syntax inside test commands also requires an explicit opt-in because it expands the trust boundary.

## What v0.6.0 changed

The M00–M05 architecture is unchanged. This release folds in the fixes that only surfaced once the orchestrator was pointed at a real repository:

- built-in default commands for the Codex, AGY and Claude bridges, so a normal run no longer depends on environment variables;
- structured AGY auditing that starts in an isolated project, removing manual per-repository read permissions;
- continuous retry and resume behaviour for transient agent failures;
- stricter classification of provider quota exhaustion versus malformed bridge output;
- live verbose progress reporting and stricter changed-file validation;
- deterministic SHA-256 identifiers for long Google Drive `appProperties` keys.

It was validated end to end against a real TargetIntel-IO milestone, covering implementation correction, deterministic gates, adversarial audit, independent review, evidence packaging and the final `READY_FOR_HUMAN_RELEASE` state.

## Why it belongs in a scientific portfolio

The project is not a claim that automation removes scientific judgment. It demonstrates the opposite: agentic workflows become more useful when scientific scope, mechanical correctness, adversarial review and human authority are represented as different responsibilities.

## Current boundary

Dev Autopilot is research-preview software. It coordinates and audits work, but never stages, commits, pushes, tags or merges product code. A human must inspect the final diff and evidence.
